findings: S5 . MINOR: the check asks 04-uiux-brief.md for a hex palette, pixel type pairs and millisecond motion values. generate_instruction.md S4 'The number rule, DECIDED' and reference/L S.L.6 forbid exactly those anywhere in the corpus, and the supplied generation_instruction_guidelines document forbids them again. The brief carries colour as family/tone/shade derived through tools/source_lint.py::colour_words, motion as character, and type exactly, which is the settled rule. The intent of S5 (values where values belong, never adjectives) is met; the enumerated examples are superseded.

S6 . MINOR: the check asks 05-backend-schema.md for a named index or constraint carrying the critical rule plus the 'app-level checks alone fail' reminder. G43 (prescription_lint) fails a named index construct, and generate_instruction.md S4 deletes that reminder at variant b and above. 05-backend-schema.md states each concurrency rule as an observable invariant instead (invariants 4, 6, 7 and the two concurrency paragraphs).

S7 . MINOR: 06-implementation-plan.md carries numbered phases with observable exit conditions and ends at accessibility hardening rather than at a deploy-and-self-test phase. '## Build plan' is not emitted at this variant (generate_instruction.md S2.1) and a self-test instruction is banned by S4.0-B, so the deploy phase would be a step nothing downstream may read.

A1 . MINOR: '## Build plan' is absent. A1 lists eleven required H2s; generate_instruction.md S2.1 retires Build plan from the baseline and reference/A S.A.7 makes '## Front-end specification' the optional eleventh, which the brief emits. window_lint (G33) and contract_lint (G4) both pass on the emitted set.

B1 . MINOR: the content-publishing row gives two roles (author, reader) and the role-fit rule says to keep the count. The brief carries five seeded roles. reference/B S.B.3 sets the enterprise band at 3 to 5, and the companion's two load-bearing separations of duty (an author never approves their own work; one principal never decides two stages) cannot be expressed with two. Recorded in spec/00-decisions.md under Roles.
B3 . MINOR: two of the three difficulty levers are present ('## Technical requirements' and '## Data model'); '## Build plan' is the third and is not baseline. Same conflict as A1, same source.

C5 . MINOR: the check asks '## Data model' to name concurrency invariants as storage-level constraints with the app-level reminder. G43 fails a named index construct in that section and S4 deletes the reminder above variant a. The section states the invariants observably instead ('Two transitions on one record from the same starting state do not both succeed ... This holds under real concurrency').

C7 . MINOR: five of the six judged sections run past the 2,500-character slice and the join runs past 9,000. generate_instruction.md S4 states plainly that the brief has no length limit, that window_lint reports past-slice as information rather than a finding, and that trimming a real rule to fit the window is the wrong trade. The tasker also asked for the cap constraints to be set aside in favour of a fuller UI/UX specification.

D4 . MINOR: one occurrence of the word grader appears in the brief, inside the verbatim Data model password block generate_instruction.md S4 requires ('so a grader can sign in'). It names no backing service and locates no checker outside the app, so it is not the harness-verifier prose class D3/D4 exist to catch. disclosure_lint (G44) passes.

RC-15 . MINOR: the loop ran four cycles rather than three. Cycle one drew the criteria from the brief; cycle two rewrote every criterion against the nineteen text rules after rubric_lint reported negations, banned adverbs and connectors; cycle three re-balanced the dimension budget and the task-completion share; cycle four confirmed clean. Recorded rather than reported as convergence.
SIGN-001 / SIGN-002 / SIGN-003 . deprecated 2026-09-15 and superseded by SIGN-004, which passes: the file carries no [signoff] table.
BENCH-002 . the task is not trivial, so the Trivial tier does not apply; BENCH-001 carries the Standard tier and passes exactly.
TAX-006 . language is python rather than any, so the any-only rule does not apply.

TAX-008 . archetype uniqueness cannot be decided from one bundle. task_code.py mint claimed governed-disclosure-platform atomically against the ledger; recorded as unverifiable from the supplied inputs, per the row's own instruction.
INST-007 . instruction.md is present, so the absent-brief rule does not apply.

COV-004 . MINOR: six of the seven spec documents are classified and used. 06-implementation-plan.md is deliberately unused, because '## Build plan' is not emitted at this variant; the exclusion is recorded in the file's own opening paragraph and in spec/00-decisions.md.

BENCH-003 / BENCH-005 / INT-007 . MINOR: difficulty is the empty placeholder the Calibration Engineer fills (TAX-010), so the turns/tokens band cannot be checked against a declared difficulty. turns_expected 200 and tokens_expected 8000000 are the top of the documented band and the ceiling BENCH-004 sets, chosen because the companion cap (config/corpus-targets.yaml companion_feature_cap) allowed ten must-have features and ten do not build in six features' time.
SVC-008 . no add-on slot is declared; the two slots are backend and storage, both core.

DEP-011 . [verifier].environment_mode is separate, so the grader runs in its own image on deku-verifier-base and the agent image owes it no pinned Python grader package. G55 RD-1 skips for the same reason.

DEP-015 / DEP-016 / DEP-017 . language is python, so the compiled-language rules (multi-stage on the Playwright base, build-resolved dependency cache, a JRE in the final stage) do not apply. The file carries no --break-system-packages and no pip fallback.
ARCH-002 / ARCH-003 . the base image is pinned by the tag python:3.12-slim-bookworm rather than by digest, so there is no digest to check for manifest-list form or traceability.

BP-004 . no build-time download carries a source-provided checksum: the NodeSource key is fetched over a verified transport and added as a signing key, which is the integrity mechanism for that repository.

BP-005 . a multi-stage build would not reduce the final image, because the grader runtime (Chromium, Playwright, the pinned Python packages) has to be present at run time rather than only at build time.
SEC-003 . no source or convention establishes non-root execution for the agent image; the agent writes to /app and installs at run time.
ENV-003 . the sources require no VOLUME in the agent image, and none is declared.
ENV-004 . no source requires an ENTRYPOINT; the image declares CMD ["sleep", "infinity"], which BP-021 and G55 RD-7 both want.

CMP-011 . MINOR: the main service publishes 4173:4173. CMP-011 reads on its own as a ban on any ports key, and CMP-022 requires main to set ports; the rationale CMP-011 gives is a sidecar binding a host port and turning a concurrent trial into a bind conflict. No sidecar publishes a port. The main mapping is the App Contract's own ${APP_PUBLIC_PORT}:4173.

BC-002 / BC-003 / BC-005 / BC-006 . the agent image runs no long-running network service of its own: CMD is sleep infinity and the app is built by the agent inside the session. The bind address, the configured port, the detached start and the production build are all carried as App Contract requirements in instruction.md, where the agent reads them.
